findings.title: A /goal kickoff clears a stopped goal's latch only in memory, so a reload before the model's set re-instates the stop on the user's new goal
findings.detail: For `paused`/`active` goals the kickoff both re-arms memory and durably clears the latch (`persistGoalState(false)`, line 1945). The new status filter excludes `blocked`, so for a goal stopped with `/goal stop` (which persists `{goal: {status: "blocked"}, stopped: true}`, lines 1918-1920) the kickoff writes nothing: `resetContinuationBudget()` (lines 1174-1176) flips `stopped` to false in memory only, while the branch's newest entry still carries the explicit `stopped: true`. Reload/resume between the kickoff and the model's `set` re-adopts that latch — `sessionStopped = stoppedFromState(data)` returns the explicit flag (lines 1025-1027, 1044) and `stopped = sessionStopped ?? false` (line 1209) makes it true again — and the `set` then bakes it into the brand-new goal via `persistGoalState(stopped ? true : undefined)` (line 1664), writing `{goal: {status: "active"}, stopped: true}`. That window is real: the kickoff only queues a `followUp` for the model (line 1950), so the `set` never lands if the run aborts/errors, if the user reloads while the message is still queued (a routine action in this repo), or if the first `set` is rejected for an invalid verify. Consequence: the user's freshly engaged goal silently never auto-checks — no turn-end verify, no continuation, footer `goal · halted — /goal resume re-arms` — and the tool result/notify attribute it to "a /goal stop or the continuation cap" affecting the new goal. The identical sequence without the intervening reload leaves the new goal armed, which is exactly the reload-dependent latch outcome this diff set out to remove (docstring, lines 1020-1024). The surrounding comments still assume otherwise: line 1927-1928 ("the kickoff is a deliberate re-engagement: re-arm it in memory AND on the branch") and line 1205-1207 ("their state entries carry no latch") are both false for a `/goal stop`ped goal, whose entry carries the latch precisely so a reload cannot resurrect it.
findings.recommendation: In the kickoff, clear the latch durably for terminal goals too, without resurrecting the objective: leave the goal's status untouched but persist the released latch (e.g. `persistGoalState(false)` for a `blocked` goal — the branch then reads `{goal: {status: "blocked"}, stopped: false}`, the status guards keep the loop down until a new goal exists, and the model's later `set` no longer inherits the superseded stop). Update the two comments that state terminal entries carry no latch / are re-armed on the branch, and add a test for stop → kickoff → reload → set asserting the new goal's entry has no `stopped` flag.

findings.title: The changed latch derivation has no direct test: `scanGoalState(...).sessionStopped` is never asserted, so the new `=== "paused"` fallback is uncovered
findings.detail: `stoppedFromState` (extensions/goal.ts:1025-1028) is the core semantic this diff changes, and `scanGoalState` (goal.ts:1035) exposes its result as `sessionStopped`. `sessionStopped` is never asserted anywhere in tests/, and `describe("scanGoalState / lastGoalSnapshot")` (tests/goal.test.ts:447-517) only covers `goal` and `hiddenByCompaction`. Every reload test writes the latch explicitly (`/goal pause` → `persistGoalState(true)`, goal.ts:1872, exercised at tests/goal.test.ts:2447), so the changed fallback `data.goal?.status === "paused"` is never reached and its true branch is invisible to the suite — a regression on that exact line fails nothing. Only the 'no latch for blocked/complete' direction is protected (tests/goal.test.ts:2496).
findings.recommendation: Add `scanGoalState` cases: `[goalState(goal({status:"paused"}))]` → `sessionStopped === true`; `status:"blocked"`/`"complete"` with no flag → `false`; a branch with no state entry → `undefined`.

findings.title: The kickoff guard this diff narrows is only tested for the `complete` case; `blocked` and the retained paused/active re-arm paths are unexercised
findings.detail: The diff changed `if (goal)` to `if (goal && (goal.status === "active" || goal.status === "paused"))` (extensions/goal.ts:1942). The only two `/goal <objective>` kickoff call sites in the suite are tests/goal.test.ts:2254 (a `complete` goal — the exclusion case) and :2277 (no goal at all). So the guard's other clauses are unpinned: a `blocked` goal falls down the same exclusion branch the new comment calls out ('finished/abandoned work'), and the true branch that must keep re-arming a `paused` or latched-`active` goal (`goal = {…active}; stopped = false; persistGoalState(false)`, goal.ts:1943-1945) is never hit. A condition typo (drop `paused`, add `blocked`) fails no test. The test also never asserts the kickoff still routes the objective to the model (`pi.sendUserMessage`), so it would still pass if that follow-up handling were removed — its assertions are only 'no entry appended' plus 'status still says (complete)'.
findings.recommendation: Extend the kickoff test: a `blocked` goal must also append nothing and stay blocked; a `paused`/latched-active goal must be re-armed in memory and on the branch (`stopped` cleared, status active). Also assert `pi.sendUserMessage` fired with the objective so the model-routing half of the kickoff is protected.

findings.title: The new "terminal goal derives no latch" reload test passes with adoption completely broken
findings.detail: The test's comment promises a true round trip ("a FRESH registration (empty memory) must reconstruct everything from that branch alone … remove the writes or the adoption and these fail"), but none of its assertions depend on the blocked goal being adopted. If `adoptBranchState`/`scanGoalState` returned no goal at all for the `{goal:{status:'blocked'}}` entry, then `goal === null` and `stopped` keeps its initial `false`: the first settle still returns `undefined` via `if (!goal || goal.status !== "active" || stopped) return` (goal.ts:1329, line 2512 passes), the set at 2513 is still allowed (only `paused` is refused, goal.ts:1647) and persists without a latch so the text still lacks "loop is STOPPED" (line 2518 passes), and the follow-up settle still runs the fresh goal's check and returns `{continue:true}` (line 2519 passes). The test therefore pins the write side and the `stoppedFromState` derivation (the pre-fix code would fail line 2518 because the adopted latch is `true`), but not the adoption of the blocked-but-unlatched snapshot that the comment claims — unlike its siblings, which each re-assert the adopted state (tests/goal.test.ts:2438 "(blocked)", 2541 "(complete)"). A regression that drops or mis-scans blocked snapshots (the goal silently disappearing on reload) is invisible here.
findings.recommendation: Assert the adopted identity/state, e.g. `expect(r.content[0].text).toContain("Goal #2 set")` (proves `goalSeq` was resumed from the adopted goal) and/or drive `/goal status` after the reload and assert it reports "(blocked)", as the stop/complete tests already do.

findings.title: `complete and blocked survive a reload as terminal states` exercises only `complete`, and every assertion also holds under the pre-diff behavior
findings.detail: The test builds only a `complete` goal (set + complete, then reload). All of its assertions — `agent_before_settle` undefined, the goal tool not re-activated, status `(complete)` — follow from the unchanged status guards (`goal.status !== "active"` at goal.ts:1329 and `g.status !== "complete"` at goal.ts:1210) and hold identically with the old latch derivation (the old code would set `stopped = true` on adoption, which changes none of these three outcomes), so it pins nothing about this diff's change. Its own comment 'Completed goals do not re-activate the goal tool; blocked ones do' is never asserted for blocked — the blocked half of the title is untested, and that activation difference is the one behavior the diff actually affects for terminal goals.
findings.recommendation: Add the blocked half (model `blocked` → reload → status `(blocked)` and `activeTools` contains the goal tool), which is the only place the blocked-vs-complete tool activation and terminal-but-unlatched adoption is pinned; or retitle to the complete case.
